sentences.text: 2. Earlier the petitioner was granted provisional bail in terms of order dated 31.01.2020 as passed in Cr. Misc. No. 67419 of 2019.
Petitioner remained in custody for about four months before granting provisional bail.

3. As per FIR, which is based upon written information of the informant namely Kamlakant Prasad Sy. DSP stating inter-alia therein that for the appointment of constables and equivalent post in terms of agreement dated 12.02.2018 executed between the Central Selection Board (Constable Appointment) (hereinafter referred as "Board") Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12)
dt.05-02-2026 and M/s. ICN (India) Pvt. Ltd. (hereinafter referred as "Company") was executed for the recruitment of constables during financial year 2017-18 & 2018-19.
It is alleged that co-accused Sunil Kumar Dhawan who happens to be the owner-cum-director of the company has authorized the manager of the company (petitioner) to execute the agreement.

In furtherance of the agreement company has to invite online application for appointment on different posts on behalf of the Board and application fee collected has to be deposited in the account of the Board within six days of its collection.

It is alleged that company has collected total of Rs.32,47,72,756/- from the applicants for the post of "constable" with respect to Advt No.02/2018 out of which the company has deposited Rs.28,97,72,756/- and the rest amount of Rs.3.5 Crores has not been deposited in the account of Board.

Similarly against Advt No.09/2019, the company has collected Rs.10,56,39,674/- against the post of "Forest Guard" and same has also not deposited in the account of the Board and as such the company failed to deposit total amount of Rs.14,06,39,674/- which was to be Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12) dt.05-02-2026 deposited latest by 07.02.2019.

The company failed to deposit aforesaid amount despite of several reminders as well as legal notices, consequent upon the informant lodged present criminal case, which has been registered as Shastri Nagar P.S. Case No.
733 of 2019 on 06.09.2029 for the offence punishable under Sections 409 and 420 of the IPC.

entities.text:

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of petitioner submitted that petitioner on behalf of company in the capacity of manager has entered into an agreement dated 12.02.2018 with the Board for collection of online applications for the post of constable and forest guard.
It is admitted position that petitioner signed agreement as authorized representative of the company in capacity of manager.

It is submitted by learned counsel that the aforesaid agreement specifically provides a room for arbitration in case of any dispute through arbitration clause no. 19 as available through agreement dated 12.02.2018 for which Board filed as Reference Case No. 10 of 2025 before this Court, where Hon'ble Court vide order dated 18.04.2025 pleased to issue notice and is pending for consideration.

It is submitted that as dispute is Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12)
dt.05-02-2026 primarily civil in nature therefore lodging of present complaint case is completely un-occasioned and unwarranted.

5. Arguing further, it is submitted that despite of knowing that entire agreement was executed with company which is duly incorporated under Indian Companies (Amendment) Act, 1952 (as amended time to time), the company was not made accused in the present case and, therefore, the allegations as raised though present FIR not appears legally sound in want of prosecution of the company being Arun Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35689715/
2 an independent body.

In support of his submission learned counsel relied upon the legal report of Hon'ble Supreme Court as available through R. Kalyani Vs. Janak C. Mehta and Others, [(2009) 1 SCC 516].
6.

entities.text: R. Kalyani Vs. Janak C. Mehta and Others, [(2009) 1 SCC 516]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted by learned counsel that petitioner paid Rs. 3.5 Crores at the time of furnishing bail bond out of Rs. 10,56,99,674/- in furtherance of Advt No. 09/2019.

It is pointed out that four different cheque covering entire amount already given by petitioner which upon presentation found dishonored and for that a separate legal proceedings under Section 138 of the N.I. Act has already Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12) dt.05-02-2026 initiated against petitioner.

It is also pointed out from the allegations as set out through written information,
that it nowhere suggest that the allegation is covering a prima-facie case for the offence punishable under Section 409 and 420 of the IPC as admittedly major amount collected by the company was already deposited with company and therefore, it cannot be said that petitioner was under intention to cheat the Board from very inception of the agreement.

While concluding the argument it is submitted that this Court cannot act like a recovery court under the threat of criminal prosecution,
particularly when the dispute primarily appears civil in nature having arbitration clause.
7. Learned APP, opposed the prayer for bail.

8. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of Board, while opposing the prayer of bail submitted that petitioner himself undertake before the Court that he would pay Rs.10,56,99,674/- and after his assurance only, he was granted provisional bail by the Hon'ble High Court through Cr. Misc. No.
67419 of 2019.
It is submitted that the petitioner accepted his liability and, therefore, he can't take u-turn.
In Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12) dt.05-02-2026 this context it is submitted that acting upon his assurance and undertaking petitioner already deposited Rs. 3.5 Crores.

However, learned counsel for the Board could not disputed the status of petitioner as manager and further that the agreement is with arbitration clause as mentioned aforesaid for which a reference case is also pending before this Court.
It is also conceded that the company as an independent body was not impleaded as an accused through present FIR.

9. This court is also aware about the fact that this is a constitutional court and cannot act like a recovery court in bail proceedings by way of imposing onerous condition which is a clear violation of legal ratio as established by Hon'ble Supreme Court through Srikant Kumar @ Shrikant Kumar Vs.
State of Bihar and Another, [2025 SCC OnLine SC 2215].

sentences.text:
Petitioner is on interim protection in view of order dated 27.04.2020, as passed by Hon'ble Supreme Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12) dt.05-02-2026 Court in SLP (CRL.) No.
2489/2021, where Hon'ble Supreme Court, set aside the order dated 31.01.2020 as passed in Cr.
Misc. No. 67419 of 2019.

11. In view of aforesaid factual submission and by taking note of fact as dispute primarily appears civil in nature, where the parties are in process to redress their dispute in terms of arbitration clause Arun Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35689715/
3 of the agreement for which the reference case is pending before this Court, coupled with the fact as agreement was executed with company, which not appears impleaded as accused and as the petitioner before granting provisional bail remains in custody for about four months, accordingly the petitioner above named, is directed to be released on bail, furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned ACJM-IV, Patna /concerned trial court where the case is pending in connection with Shastri Nagar P.S. Case No. 733 of 2019 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C./ Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
12. Petitioner is directed to furnish bail bonds and Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.67419 of 2019(12) dt.05-02-2026 sureties within three weeks of this order, before learned trial court/
concerned court, in terms of order as directed above.
